definition: An international standard for managing information security in an organization.
exampleSentence: Our company earned ISO 27001 certification after a year of hard preparation.

fullForm: National Institute of Standards and Technology
definition: A US agency whose frameworks are widely used to organize security work.
exampleSentence: We organized our security roadmap around the NIST guidelines for risk management.

fullForm: Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard
definition: A security standard for companies that store or process card payments.
exampleSentence: Passing the PCI DSS audit was required before we could accept credit cards.

definition: A report that shows a service provider handles customer data securely.
exampleSentence: Many clients ask for our SOC 2 report before they sign a contract.

fullForm: Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act
definition: A US law that protects the privacy of patients' health information.
exampleSentence: The hospital app must follow HIPAA rules when it stores medical records.

definition: A public knowledge base that lists attacker tactics and techniques.
exampleSentence: The red team described each step of the test using MITRE ATT&CK names.

definition: A community that publishes free guides and tools for web application security.
exampleSentence: Our developers use the OWASP cheat sheets when they build login pages.

definition: Detailed guides that show how to configure systems securely.
exampleSentence: The administrator applied the CIS Benchmarks to every new Linux server.

definition: A structured set of guidelines used to build and improve a security program.
exampleSentence: We chose a security framework that fits the size of our small company.

definition: The way an organization sets rules and decides who is responsible for what.
exampleSentence: Good governance makes sure that someone owns every security decision.

definition: A document that lists known risks, their owners and the plans to handle them.
exampleSentence: Every new project must add its main concerns to the risk register.

definition: The maximum time a system can be down before the damage becomes unacceptable.
exampleSentence: The business set an RTO of four hours for the online shop.

definition: The maximum amount of data, measured in time, that a company can afford to lose.
exampleSentence: With an RPO of one hour, we must back up the database every hour.

definition: Sorting data into levels, such as public or secret, to decide how to protect it.
exampleSentence: Data classification tells staff which documents may be shared outside the company.

definition: Any data that can identify a person, such as a name or an ID number.
exampleSentence: Never paste PII into a public chatbot or a shared online document.

definition: The rules that say how long data must be kept before it is deleted.
exampleSentence: Our data retention policy requires us to delete old logs after one year.

definition: The practice of keeping personal and business data safe from loss or misuse.
exampleSentence: Data protection training is mandatory for every person who handles customer files.

definition: Building privacy protection into a product from the start.
exampleSentence: Privacy by design means the app collects only the data it really needs.

definition: Employees' knowledge of common threats and the safe way to behave.
exampleSentence: Regular security awareness sessions teach staff how to spot strange emails.

definition: A discussion-based practice where a team walks through a made-up incident.
exampleSentence: During the tabletop exercise, the managers practiced how to announce a data breach.

definition: The risk that comes from vendors, partners or suppliers who access your systems.
exampleSentence: Third-party risk is high because one supplier has full access to our network.

definition: A review of a supplier's security before and during the business relationship.
exampleSentence: The vendor assessment showed that the supplier did not encrypt customer files.

definition: Apps or devices that employees use at work without approval from the IT team.
exampleSentence: Shadow IT grows fast when employees find official tools too slow or limited.

definition: A complete list of all hardware, software and data a company owns.
exampleSentence: An accurate asset inventory is the first step of every security project.

definition: A formal review that checks whether systems and processes follow security rules.
exampleSentence: The external security audit found two serious gaps in our access process.

definition: A comparison between the current security level and the level that is required.
exampleSentence: The gap analysis showed we still lack logging for our cloud accounts.

definition: A formal approval to break a security rule for a limited time and reason.
exampleSentence: Each policy exception must be approved by a manager and expires after thirty days.

definition: The careful research a company does before trusting a partner or buying a product.
exampleSentence: Proper due diligence would have revealed that the vendor had been hacked before.

definition: The idea that data is subject to the laws of the country where it is stored.
exampleSentence: Data sovereignty rules require us to keep citizen records on servers in our country.

definition: A financial penalty from an authority when a company breaks data or security laws.
exampleSentence: A heavy regulatory fine pushed the company to invest in better protection.

definition: The duty to inform authorities and affected people after a data breach.
exampleSentence: Our legal team prepared the breach notification within the required seventy-two hours.

definition: A developer or employee who promotes good security habits inside their own team.
exampleSentence: Each squad has a security champion who reviews risky pull requests.

definition: An insurance policy that covers financial losses caused by cyber incidents.
exampleSentence: Cyber insurance paid for part of the recovery costs after the ransomware attack.

definition: A plan that shows which security improvements will be made and when.
exampleSentence: The security roadmap for next year includes passwordless login and better logging.

definition: A clear goal that a security control should achieve.
exampleSentence: Each control objective in the audit has evidence that proves it is met.

definition: The practice of protecting information in any form from unauthorized access or loss.
exampleSentence: Information security covers paper documents as well as servers and cloud storage.

definition: The ability to keep operating and recover quickly while under cyber attack.
exampleSentence: Cyber resilience means that customers barely notice when one system goes down.

definition: A European directive that sets stricter cybersecurity rules for important organizations.
exampleSentence: Our energy partner must follow NIS2 and report serious incidents quickly.

definition: Measurements, like time to patch, that show how well security work is going.
exampleSentence: We track security metrics every month and share them with the leadership team.

definition: The structure of roles, decisions and oversight that guides security in a company.
exampleSentence: Strong security governance means that the board understands the main cyber risks.
